name: Queens Who Ruled in Their Own Right
description: Pharaohs, empresses and queens who held real power, from Hatshepsut to Elizabeth II, and how each won, kept or lost a crown.

checkpoints.name: Queens of the ancient world
checkpoints.note: Hatshepsut takes the pharaoh's crown, Tomyris is said to defeat Cyrus, Cleopatra holds Egypt against Rome, Boudica leads a revolt against Roman rule in Britain, and Zenobia challenges Rome from Palmyra.

checkpoints.name: Medieval queens
checkpoints.note: Wu Zetian rules China, Eleanor of Aquitaine shapes two kingdoms and Tamar of Georgia leads her country at its height.

checkpoints.name: Renaissance queens
checkpoints.note: Isabella unites Spain, Jane Grey and Mary I reign in turn, Elizabeth I governs for decades, Mary of Scotland loses her throne, and Nzinga fights the Portuguese.

checkpoints.name: Enlightenment queens
checkpoints.note: Anne, Maria Theresa and Catherine the Great hold great states together through wars and reform in Europe.

checkpoints.name: Empresses and resisters
checkpoints.note: Victoria rules an empire, Cixi directs China, and Lakshmibai, Ranavalona and Yaa Asantewaa resist foreign rule. Wilhelmina takes the Dutch throne in 1890 and keeps her country neutral through the First World War.

checkpoints.name: A modern monarchy
checkpoints.note: Elizabeth II reigns for seventy years, longer than any British monarch before her.
